failing.note: OpenSSL QUICv1/TLS1.3 handshake succeeds from the same host, so this is a netz client interop issue rather than reachability. The netz client receives no server response across five retries.

root_cause_analysis: The quic.tech server responds with an ACK-only Initial packet number zero followed by an Initial packet number one carrying CRYPTO offset zero.

InitialResponseFilter currently rejects the ACK-only packet; openInitialCryptoFlightFrom then expects packet number zero and discards the CRYPTO packet number one, so the ServerHello is never processed.

Accepting the ACK-only packet unconditionally was tested and reintroduced the documented split-ClientHello deadlock: the client leaves the PTO loop and stops retransmitting the missing ClientHello fragments.

A correct fix must authenticate and accept the first ACK-only Initial, process coalesced or subsequent Initial CRYPTO packets, and retain ClientHello retransmission when the initial flight deadline expires.
